title: Compelling Another to Commit Crime

source.release: 2026 Criminal Jury Instructions (as adopted by the Judicial Council, February 2026)

body: If the defendant forced another person to commit a crime by threatening, menacing, commanding, or coercing that person, then the defendant is guilty of the crime that the defendant forced the other person to commit.

bench_notes.text: The court has a sua sponte duty to instruct on the theory of liability advanced by the prosecution. (See *People v. Beeman* (1984) 35 Cal.3d 547, 560–561 [199 Cal.Rptr. 60, 674 P.2d 1318] [sua sponte duty to instruct on aiding and abetting].)
